advances: An exact test for this two-parameter stochastic-capacity motion in a specified tetrahedral cut stratum; no assertion that the strict comparison always holds and no result about actual mixed-fiber cap budgets.

proof:
A proper cut crosses the interior, so its section centroid is strictly positive in all coordinates. For a full row the probability derivatives in raw margin variables are $\nabla P(c_i)=3f_i b$. Indeed, for the uniform barycentric variable the first variation is integration of the margin velocity over the proper section with its coarea density. The density of $c_i\cdot U$ at zero is $3f_i$: writing $E_j=G U_j$ with $G$ independent of $U$ and gamma of shape four gives $\mathbb E(1/G)=1/3$. Threshold stationarity of $t/F_i(t)^{1/3}$ gives $3P_i=t_i F_{X_i}'(t_i)=3t_i f_i$. In the same coarea formula, varying $X_i$ with threshold fixed changes $F_{X_i}(t_i)$ by $-3f_i b\cdot\Delta X_i$. The capacity gradient is therefore $P_i^{-1/3}b$ after the minimizing threshold, whose first-order term vanishes. In particular the normalized objective weights of the full rows are $P_i^{1/3}$, and their cuts are stationary among margins through $b$ because their probability gradients are proportional to $b$.

Apply the proof of 27d3881f8bfc290c to the captured central pair $\ell,m$ of $y$. Its tested vector is proportional to $v$ (the coordinates there are $3b_m,-3b_\ell$), so $v^{\mathsf T}H_y v<0$. The complementary orientation of $x$ has the same proper section and section centroid, and captures this same pair. Since $P(-c)=1-P(c)$ at a proper cut, the Hessian reverses sign under that orientation, giving $v^{\mathsf T}H_xv>0$ for the original $x$. Both signs apply also when one or both pair coordinates are exactly $1/3$.

Apply f8cc9b4619513ed5 to the full rows at their proper thresholds. Its normalized margins are $c_i/t_i$, with Hessians $t_i^2 H_i$ by degree-zero homogeneity of $P$. As $b\cdot v=0$, its correcting shift is exactly $\kappa_i$, with the raw factor $t_i^2$. Multiplying its capacity Hessian identity by the weight $P_i^{1/3}$ and using $P_i/t_i=f_i$ gives
$$
P_i^{1/3}(v+\kappa_i\mathbf1)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\phi_3(X_i)(v+\kappa_i\mathbf1)
=-\frac{v^{\mathsf T}H_i v}{3 f_i}.
$$

On the one-zero face, 15649c49010660b8 gives $\phi_3(z)$ as the geometric mean of its three positive entries. Let $\omega_z$ be its normalized objective weight. Transferring any positive-support entry between that row and a full row in both signs gives $\omega_z\phi_3(z)/(3z_j)=b_j$ at stationarity for $j\ne h$. Hence $w=\omega_z\phi_3(z)/3>0$ gives the asserted form of $z$, and differentiation of the geometric mean gives the weighted Hessian $(bb^{\mathsf T}/3-\operatorname{diag}(b_j^2))/w$ on its positive support, with $b$ restricted to this support. Its quadratic value on $v$ is $-2b_\ell^2 b_m^2/w$. All three capacity functions are degree-one homogeneous on their faces, so radial vectors are annihilated by their Hessians.

The stated changes sum to zero by $x+y+z=\mathbf1$; they preserve the hole since $v_h=z_h=0$, and for sufficiently small parameters of either sign all the other originally positive entries remain positive. The first derivative vanishes by stationarity. Discarding the radial terms using their Hessian kernels and adding the two full-row values and the one-zero-row value yields the displayed quadratic. For fixed $\beta$ it is maximized at $\alpha=-C\beta/(A+C)$, with value $(B-AC/(A+C))\beta^2$. This proves the equivalence and excludes a local maximum if the strict comparison holds.
statement:
Let $\Delta_3$ have the uniform probability measure on barycentric coordinates $U$, and let $\phi_3(X)=\inf_{t>0:F_X(t)>0}t/F_X(t)^{1/3}$ with $F_X(t)=\Pr(X\cdot U\le t)$. Consider a column-stochastic configuration of two positive rows $x,y$ and a one-zero row $z$ with hole $h$, so $x+y+z=\mathbf1$, stationary for a positively weighted sum of these capacities on the face of its positive entries. Any identically zero row is fixed. Assume the full rows have proper minimizing thresholds $t_i$ and strict quadrilateral cuts, capturing $\{h,j\}$ for $x$ and the complementary pair $\{\ell,m\}$ for $y$, with common actual barycentric section centroid $b$, $b_h>1/3$ and $b_i\le1/3$ for $i\ne h$. Normalize the common weighted full-row gradient to $b$. Then for some $w>0$ the zero row has $z_i=w/b_i$ for $i\ne h$.

For the full rows write $X_x=x$, $X_y=y$, $P_i=F_{X_i}(t_i)$ and $c_i=t_i\mathbf1-X_i$ for $i=x,y$, and $H_i$ be the Hessian at $c_i$ of $P(c)=\Pr(\sum_j c_jE_j\ge0)$ for independent unit exponentials. Let $f_i$ denote the density of $\sum_j(c_i)_j E_j$ at zero, so $f_i=P_i/t_i$. Put $v=b_m e_\ell-b_\ell e_m$, $\kappa_i=t_i^2(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}H_i v)/(3P_i)$, and
$$
A=\frac{v^{\mathsf T}H_xv}{3f_x},\qquad
B=-\frac{v^{\mathsf T}H_yv}{3f_y},\qquad
C=\frac{2b_\ell^2 b_m^2}{w}.
$$
All three constants are strictly positive. For any real $\alpha,\beta$ put $K=\alpha\kappa_x+\beta\kappa_y$. There are actual two-sided feasible straight row changes
$$
\Delta x=\alpha(v+\kappa_x\mathbf1)-Kx,\quad
\Delta y=\beta(v+\kappa_y\mathbf1)-Ky,\quad
\Delta z=-(\alpha+\beta)v-Kz .
$$
Their exact weighted second variation is $-A\alpha^2+B\beta^2-C(\alpha+\beta)^2$. Some direction in this family has strictly positive second variation if and only if $B>AC/(A+C)$, equivalently $1/B<1/A+1/C$.
title: A tetrahedral corrected pair has an exact joint funding criterion
